mgmt_bio.text: Belen Garijo was appointed chief executive of Sanofi in February 2026, replacing Paul Hudson, who had led the company since 2019 and was ousted after a major increase in research spending failed to deliver rapid results. She becomes Sanofi's first female leader, arriving from Merck KGaA, where she had served as CEO and Chair of the Executive Board since 2021, and returning to a company where she previously spent 15 years leading the integration of Genzyme after its acquisition, serving as VP of Pharmaceutical Operations for Europe and Canada, and sitting on the Executive Committee; earlier in her career she worked in R&D at Abbott Laboratories. Sanofi said her priority will be to strengthen the productivity, governance and innovation capacity of R&D. Sanofi shares fell nearly 6% on the announcement, with some analysts citing her relatively low profile.
